idiom_name: framework callback registration: function pointer + userdata (GLib main loop, qsort comparator)
implementation_notes: C has no language support for the pattern: you declare a callback type, register a function pointer together with a userdata void* - or a small struct of function pointers when several callbacks share state - and the library's loop calls it when it chooses. GLib's GMainLoop dispatches GSource callbacks registered with g_timeout_add/g_idle_add and signals connected with g_signal_connect, and even a single library function such as qsort takes the comparison function and calls it per element, so the classic 'framework base class' is replaced by an explicit ops struct whose function pointers you fill in. Hand-written registration is still justified when the API is a plain C library that cannot own your state, but all dispatch bookkeeping (source ids, cancellation, locking) becomes yours.
pitfalls: A callback invoked after the object it points at was freed is the default failure mode: keep the GSource id and remove it with g_source_remove() when the owning object is finalized, or hold a strong reference in the callback.

The userdata pointer is untyped and unattributed: every callback must re-establish which struct it receives, and callbacks attached to a main context may run on another thread, so shared state needs its own locking.
